name: Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition

Optimal.Notes: This profile targets a stable 30 fps locked at 40 Hz for smooth pacing, with textures and reflections bumped up for a noticeably better-looking city. View Distance at 20 is a reasonable compromise between draw distance and CPU overhead — raise it cautiously if frame rate holds.

profiles.Summary: Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition runs on the Steam Deck via Proton with a gold/trending-platinum ProtonDB rating, meaning most players get it working well with some tweaking. The game is notoriously CPU-heavy and poorly optimized even on PC, so expect frame-rate variability in dense city areas even at reduced settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from GTA IV's well-known PC optimization characteristics, its minimum PC GPU requirements (roughly GTX 7900-era, well below Deck capability), and the Deck hardware profile. On first run, check the frame rate in Algonquin (the densest borough) and lower View Distance and Detail Distance first if it stutters.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and upscale with FSR to ease GPU load; View Distance and Detail Distance are the biggest CPU/GPU cost levers in GTA IV — keep them low. The 8 W TDP and 40 Hz refresh rate together extend battery significantly while keeping gameplay comfortable.

KnownIssues: GTA IV is infamously CPU-bound and poorly optimized; frame drops in dense Liberty City areas are common even on powerful hardware.
The game may require the Social Club / Rockstar Games Launcher to initialize, which can cause launch issues under Proton — GE-Proton often helps.
Mouse/keyboard input may be needed for initial launcher setup; partial controller support means some menus may not be fully navigable with a gamepad.
The in-game frame limiter and v-sync can conflict with Deck system-level frame caps, causing stutter — prefer the Deck QAM frame limiter over the in-game one.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Night Shadows remain off as they carry a heavy CPU cost disproportionate to visual gain on this hardware; all other settings are pushed as high as the Deck can realistically sustain. Expect dips toward 30 fps in the densest parts of Algonquin — GTA IV's CPU bottleneck is unavoidable.

Optimal.Notes: A stable 30 fps cap with a 12 W TDP gives a good balance of visual quality and battery life; Texture Quality at High makes the biggest visual improvement for minimal GPU cost, while keeping View Distance moderate prevents the CPU from becoming a bottleneck.

profiles.Summary: Grand Theft Auto IV runs on the Steam Deck via Proton at a playable but inconsistent frame rate; the game's notoriously CPU-heavy engine and poor PC optimization make it one of the more demanding titles relative to its age, and the Deck's Zen 2 CPU can struggle in dense traffic areas. ProtonDB reporters trend platinum, suggesting it boots and plays well with the right Proton version, though GTA IV's built-in graphics settings need careful tuning to avoid CPU bottlenecks.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from GTA IV's notorious PC optimization characteristics, its minimum/recommended PC requirements relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, and the general ProtonDB gold/platinum trend. On first launch, check the frame rate in Algonquin (the dense city island) and lower View Distance and Detail Distance immediately if it drops below your target; those two sliders are the primary performance levers in this engine.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render resolution dropped to 960x600 with FSR upscaling to ease both CPU and GPU load; View Distance and Detail Distance are the biggest performance levers in GTA IV and should be reduced first if frame rate dips below 30.

KnownIssues: GTA IV's engine is infamously CPU-bound and poorly optimized; expect frame dips in dense traffic or cutscenes even at low GPU settings.
The in-game video settings menu can be confusing and some options (e.g. Night Shadows, Reflection Resolution) have outsized performance costs.
Social Club / Rockstar Games Launcher overlay may cause launch issues; disabling it via launch options is commonly recommended.
Controller layout may require manual Steam Input configuration as partial controller support is listed and some UI elements expect mouse/keyboard.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Targeting 40 fps at 40 Hz for the smoothest experience the Deck can realistically sustain; GTA IV's CPU bottleneck means View Distance above 30 will cause dips, and Anti-Aliasing is left off as it is extremely expensive in this engine for minimal visual gain.
